newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian metal union cancels wage contracts.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian metal union cancels wage contracts.

text.p: The large Bavarian branch of the IG Metall engineering and metal industry trade union on Friday said it was cancelling existing wage contracts with effect from January 31.
The regional trade union committee had met to decide future action after the break-down on Wednesday of national talks with employers over planned cuts to sick pay.
Its decision to cancel current wage contracts opens the way for the union to hold full strikes in the region from the end of February.
IG Metall is demanding that employers maintain sick payments at their current 100 percent of salary and do not implement a newly-passed law allowing them to cut payments to 80 percent.

The Bavarian trade union committee, which represents some 650,000 of the total 3.5 million workers employed in the sector, is the first of the IG Metall regions to go as close to full strike action as cancelling wage contracts.
The move follows Thursday's wave of wildcat protests against the planned cuts by hundreds of thousands of metal and engineering workers around the country.
The protests went ahead despite pledges by employers not to implement the 20 percent sick pay reduction until wider agreement with unions had been reached.

Separately, the German metal and engineering employers federation in the steel-producing region of North-Rhine Westphalia said on Friday they were taking the issue of planned sick pay cuts to a regional court.
The employers federation said it wanted to establish that the new law could be applied to the 800,000 workers in the metal sector in North-Rhine Westphalia.
